sheet-2.description: The business centre of Hammonton, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. The sheet is centred on Bellevue Avenue, which runs up the page from North and South Railroad Avenues and the tracks of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad) at the bottom to North and South Third Streets at the top, between East Orchard Street on the left edge and Peach Street on the right. Second Street and North and South Egg Harbor Road cross it, Horton Street runs west from Bellevue, and Central Avenue leaves Bellevue diagonally toward the upper right. Bellevue Avenue is lined with brick and frame stores, many marked as stores with offices or halls above: the Peoples Bank, Hammonton Auto Station (a garage with a steel truss roof), Bellevue Hall, a hardware and paints store, moving picture theatres, a bank and drug store near Egg Harbor Road, and the Hammonton Hotel. West of Bellevue are the Independent Fire Co. No. 1 house, the Hammonton Damp Wash Laundry, a bottling works and a garage; east of Vine Street are the town hall, the library, the post office, Moose Hall and the Jackson Hotel. Along the railroad stand the passenger station, the freight house and platform, garages and a filling station. Water pipes with their sizes, hydrants and the widths of the streets are marked throughout.
notes: North Railroad Avenue is modern Railroad Avenue and South Railroad Avenue is modern Front Street; Bellevue Avenue south of the tracks is modern 12th Street.
Horton Street, Central Avenue and Bellevue Avenue meet at one junction north of Second Street.

50 ft. Downtown: Bellevue Av between N/S 3rd St and N/S Railroad Av, Orchard to Peach, Horton, Central Av, N/S 2nd, N/S Egg Harbor Rd. N Railroad Av is modern Railroad Avenue, S Railroad Av is Front Street, Bellevue south of the tracks is 12th Street.

sheet-3.description: The blocks south of the railroad at the centre of Hammonton, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Twelfth Street runs up the middle of the sheet from North and South Grand Streets at the bottom to North and South Railroad Avenues at the top; West Orchard Street is on the left edge and Passmore Avenue on the right, drawn with only its west side. Between them run North and South Washington Avenues, the tracks of the Atlantic City Railroad (Philadelphia and Reading Railway) with sidings, North and South West End Avenues, Lincoln Street and Woodman Avenue. The northern blocks are industrial: Consolidated Pants Co. factory, Hammonton Glass Co., Hammonton Lime and Cement Co., Hammonton Auction House, William Penn Tapestry Mills, auto storage and repair shops, and the Hammonton Lumber Co. with its sheds along the siding. By the tracks are the passenger depot, freight house and a writing room. South of the railroad stand the Hammonton Water Works pumping station, the Atlantic City Electric Co. plant with two gas holders and a transformer yard, and the Standard Oil Co. tanks; Hotel Columbia and a storage building face North West End Avenue. The southern blocks between Lincoln Street, Woodman Avenue and Grand Street are filled with frame dwellings.
notes: South Railroad Avenue is modern Front Street; North and South Washington Avenues are modern North Washington Street and Washington Street South.
The water works pumping station is lettered with a reference to Sheet No. 1 for its report.

50 ft. 12th St from N/S Railroad Av to N/S Grand, W Orchard to Passmore: Washington Av, West End Av, Lincoln, Woodman; railroad yards, gas works. Passmore is drawn with only its west edge; its junctions are carried from sheet 8 (block corners, manual/sheet-3.json).

sheet-4.description: The north-western residential edge of Hammonton, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Fairview Avenue runs up the left third of the sheet from North Third Street at the bottom to Fourth Street at the top; to its right are East Pratt Street, East French Street (marked not open north of Packard) and East Pleasant Street along the right edge, crossed by North Packard Street (continuing west of Fairview as a road) and Tilton Street between Pratt and Pleasant. Most of the sheet is open land in large blocks numbered 41 to 43, with scattered frame dwellings, sheds and a pigeon house along Fairview Avenue and Packard Street; the lots west of Fairview are marked no exposure. Denser rows of dwellings face Tilton Street, East French and East Pleasant Streets, and North Third Street along the bottom edge, where there are stores and an automobile building near Cottage Street.
notes: Tilton Street between Pratt and French Streets is modern Mount Carmel Lane.
East French Street is marked not open north of Tilton Street.
Fourth Street is drawn straight; the modern North 4th Street curves away from it and was not used for control.

100 ft. Fairview Av to E Pleasant St, 4th St to N 3rd St: N Packard, Tilton, E Pratt, E French. Tilton between Pratt and French is modern Mount Carmel Lane. 4th St drawn straight where the modern street curves; left out.

sheet-5.description: North-central Hammonton between East Pleasant Street and Grape Street, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Bellevue Avenue runs up the middle from North and South Third Streets at the bottom to Fourth Street and Valley Avenue at the top, crossed by North and South Packard Streets; Tilton Street runs from East Pleasant to Bellevue, and Orchard, Vine and Peach Streets run up the lower and right parts of the sheet, with Central Avenue cutting across the lower right corner. The northern half is lightly built: large blocks with dwellings, a poultry farm and the large factory of Wm. B. Kessler, clothing manufacturing, on East Pleasant Street. The southern half holds the town's institutions: the W. E. Crane lumber yard with its sawdust pile, St. Joseph's Parochial School, the First Methodist Episcopal Church, the public park, the First Presbyterian Church, the Baptist Church, the Hammonton Public Schools, the Hammonton Junior High School of 1925 with its gymnasium and auditorium, the athletic field, a Masonic hall and the Universalist Church near Central Avenue.
notes: The modern North 4th Street and East Pleasant Street junction lies about 11 m from the drawn one and was rejected.
A short street along the north side of the public park joins Bellevue Avenue and Vine Street; modern Vine Street now ends there, so that junction was left out.
100 ft. E Pleasant to Grape, 4th St/Valley Av to N/S 3rd: N/S Packard, Tilton, Orchard, Bellevue, Vine, Peach; public schools, athletic field.

sheet-6.description: The eastern edge of north Hammonton, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Grape Street runs up the left edge from South Third Street to Valley Avenue along the top; Broadway crosses the upper right corner. Central Avenue runs diagonally across the sheet from the lower left toward the upper right, and Maple Avenue and Walnut Avenue run from it down to South Third Street, which bends across the lower part of the sheet; a short Cherry Street appears at the bottom. Apart from rows of frame dwellings along Grape Street, Valley Avenue, Central Avenue and the lower end of Maple Avenue, the sheet is made up of long narrow farm lots in blocks 90 to 93 and 104, with poultry houses, poultry farms and hen houses. The right edge and the strip toward Broadway are marked no exposure.
notes: Maple Avenue is modern Maple Street and Walnut Avenue is modern Walmer Street.
The north-east quarter towards Broadway has no control point.
100 ft. Grape St to Broadway, Valley Av to S 3rd: Central Av, Maple Av (Maple Street), Walnut Av (modern Walmer Street); poultry farms. NE quarter (towards Broadway) has no control.

sheet-7.description: The western half of central Hammonton, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Rows run across the sheet from North Third Street at the top through Elm and Horton Streets, North Second Street, North Egg Harbor Road, the tracks of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad, North Railroad Avenue, North Washington Avenue, the Atlantic City Railroad (Philadelphia and Reading), North West End Avenue and Messina Avenue to North Grand Street at the bottom. Fairview Avenue and Thirteenth Street are on the left edge and East and West Orchard Streets on the right; Cottage Street, East and West Pratt Street, East French Street, East and West Pleasant Street and Jacobs Avenue run up the sheet between them. Most blocks are filled with frame dwellings. Industry lies along the two railroads: the Hammonton Manufacturing Co., K. Skinner and Son cut glass factory, Anderson's mill with grain and feed warehouse, the Hammonton Building Material Co. concrete block works and Hammonton Bottling Co. on a spur track, E. Prichard canning factory, the South Jersey Laundry Co., Enterprise Cut Glass Co., the Figueroa Cut Glass Co., a garment company and Demarco potato warehouse. Near North Third Street stand St. Joseph's Roman Catholic Church and M. Waldman's pants factory.
notes: West Pratt Street between North Railroad Avenue and North Washington Avenue is modern Somerby Street.
Jacobs Avenue is modern Jacobs Street; North Washington Avenue is modern North Washington Street.

100 ft. Fairview Av/13th St to Orchard, N 3rd to N Grand: Elm, Horton, N 2nd, N Egg Harbor Rd, N Railroad Av, N Washington, N West End, Messina, Cottage, Pratt, French, Pleasant, Jacobs. W Pratt between Railroad Av and Washington is modern Somerby Street.

sheet-8.description: The south-eastern part of central Hammonton, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Rows run across the sheet from South Third Street at the top through South Second Street, the slanting South Egg Harbor Road, the tracks of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad, South Railroad Avenue, South Washington Avenue, the Atlantic City Railroad and Lincoln Street to South Grand Street at the bottom. Peach Street and Passmore Avenue are on the left edge and Eleventh Street on the right; Grape Street, Cherry Street (continued south of Egg Harbor Road as Line Street), Peressy Street and Maple Avenue run up the upper half, and Walnut Avenue enters at the top right. The blocks north of Egg Harbor Road hold dwellings, Johnston's greenhouses, hen houses and Blair's laundry; along Egg Harbor Road are the Gulf Refining Co., a garage and the Hammonton barracks of the New Jersey State Police with a road department store house. Between the railroads a wye of the West Jersey and Seashore track crosses open block 87. Along Passmore Avenue stand the Hammonton Grain Co. warehouse, the Sinclair Refining Co., the Littlefield Ice and Coal Co. and the Central Atlantic States Service Corp. ice plant. The south-eastern blocks are mostly empty.
notes: Peressy Street is modern Pressey Street; South Railroad Avenue is modern Front Street; Maple Avenue is Maple Street and Walnut Avenue is Walmer Street.
Grand Street South / Passmore Avenue and Line Street / Washington Street South were detected 7 to 10 m off the fit and rejected.
Lincoln Street east of Line Street is a modern extension; that junction was left out.

100 ft. Peach to 11th St, S 3rd to S Grand: S 2nd, S Egg Harbor Rd, S Railroad Av (Front Street), S Washington, Lincoln; Grape, Cherry/Line, Peressy (Pressey Street), Maple Av (Maple Street), Walnut Av (Walmer Street), Passmore.

sheet-9-1.description: The south-western residential and farm edge of Hammonton, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left; the part covers the sheet above a heavy dividing line. North Grand Street runs across the top from Thirteenth Street on the left; on the right West French Street, West Pleasant Street and Jacobs Avenue run down the sheet, crossed by North Madison Avenue, North Monroe Avenue and North First Road. Chew Road runs diagonally from the left edge down toward the lower right. Large block 58 between Thirteenth Street and West French Street is almost empty, with a few dwellings along its edges; blocks 59, 60, 65, 66, 71 and 72 to the right hold frame dwellings and a fruit warehouse. Dwellings line Thirteenth Street and Chew Road, and the land west of Thirteenth Street is marked no exposure.
notes: West French Street is modern Wilbur Avenue.
Jacobs Avenue is marked not open beyond North Madison Avenue.

100 ft. Two parts divided by a heavy line: part 1 N Grand to N 1st Rd and Chew Rd, 13th St to Jacobs (W French St is modern Wilbur Avenue); part 2 is the strip of Chew Rd and 13th St to N 1st Rd further south-west, drawn displaced on the page (helmert on two 13th St junctions).

sheet-9-2.description: A strip of the south-western outskirts of Hammonton drawn below the heavy line on sheet 9, at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. It continues Chew Road and Thirteenth Street further south-west than the upper part of the sheet and is drawn displaced on the page. Chew Road crosses the strip diagonally; Thirteenth Street runs down from it to North First Road near the bottom edge. The land is sparsely built: frame dwellings and sheds along Chew Road and Thirteenth Street, a public school on North First Road at the left, and open blocks 55 to 57 and 77 to 78 marked no exposure or vacant beyond.
notes: Placed by a helmert transformation from two junctions on Thirteenth Street only; low confidence.

100 ft. Two parts divided by a heavy line: part 1 N Grand to N 1st Rd and Chew Rd, 13th St to Jacobs (W French St is modern Wilbur Avenue); part 2 is the strip of Chew Rd and 13th St to N 1st Rd further south-west, drawn displaced on the page (helmert on two 13th St junctions).

sheet-10-1.description: The southern part of Hammonton between Jacobs Avenue and Line Street, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Rows cross the sheet from North and South Grand Streets at the top through North and South Madison Avenues and North and South Monroe Avenues to North and South First Roads; Jacobs Avenue, West Orchard Street, Twelfth Street, Passmore Avenue and Line Street run up the sheet. The northern blocks 61 to 76 are residential, with long rows of small dwellings on South Madison Avenue and a water works stand pipe on West Orchard Street. Below First Road the land opens out: the Wilson-Collins Co. memorials works, scattered dwellings and hen houses, and Greenmount Cemetery along the right side, with Chew Road crossing the lower left corner. The lower right corner of the sheet is a separate inset (part 2).
notes: Chew Road is drawn about 15 m from the modern road and was not used for control.

100 ft. Part 1 Grand St to Chew Rd, Jacobs to Line St (Greenmount Cemetery); part 2 inset at lower right: Fairview Av/13th St at the railroad and N Egg Harbor Rd, Caldwell Av, Hammonton Macaroni Factory (helmert on two 13th St points). Chew Rd drawn about 15 m from the modern road; left out.

sheet-10-2.description: An inset in the lower right corner of sheet 10, at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left, showing the area west of Fairview Avenue and Thirteenth Street where they cross the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad, at the western end of North Egg Harbor Road. Fairview Avenue runs down the right edge to the railroad and Thirteenth Street continues it below; Caldwell Avenue runs down from the top, and North Egg Harbor Road runs west from Thirteenth Street below the tracks. Railroad Avenue and North Washington Avenue are lettered at the right edge. The inset shows a few dwellings in block 54, the Hammonton Macaroni Factory, a garage and a hotel in block 55, and land marked no exposure to the west.
notes: Placed by a helmert transformation from two points on the line of Fairview Avenue and Thirteenth Street (the North Washington Street junction and the rail crossing); low confidence.
The modern Egg Harbor Road junctions here lie 8 m and more from the drawn ones and were not used.

100 ft. Part 1 Grand St to Chew Rd, Jacobs to Line St (Greenmount Cemetery); part 2 inset at lower right: Fairview Av/13th St at the railroad and N Egg Harbor Rd, Caldwell Av, Hammonton Macaroni Factory (helmert on two 13th St points). Chew Rd drawn about 15 m from the modern road; left out.

sheet-11-1.description: The northern outskirts of Hammonton along Bellevue Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Bellevue Avenue runs up the sheet from Valley Avenue and Fourth Street at the bottom; Fifth Street (marked not open) runs west from it and Liberty Street east to Peach and Grape Streets. The land is mostly in large blocks 46, 47, 49, 50, 102 and 48 with frame dwellings, coops and poultry farms; the lots east of Grape Street are marked no exposure. The upper right of the sheet is a separate inset (part 2) and the strip below Valley Avenue on the right is a further displaced strip of lots (not placed).
notes: Fifth Street is modern North Liberty Street and Liberty Street is South Liberty Street; the drawn spacing to Liberty Street disagrees with the modern street by about 20 m, so the Liberty junctions were left out.
Peach Street is marked not open north of the poultry farm.
Junctions along Valley Avenue fit only at about 3.76 px/ft against 3.93 for the scale bar; the second pass holds this part to the atlas scale.

100 ft. Three parts: part 1 Bellevue to Grape, 5th St/Liberty to Valley Av (Liberty junctions left out: drawn spacing disagrees with modern South Liberty Street by about 20 m; the sheet fits only at about 3.76 px/ft); part 2 inset: Caldwell (Colwell) and Fairview Avs between N 2nd and N 3rd; part 3 strip of lots on the north side of Valley Av east of Grape, drawn displaced below a heavy line, not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: strip of lots on the north side of Valley Avenue east of Grape Street (block 48, house numbers 231-383), drawn displaced below a heavy line (no street junction; Valley Avenue frontage only; needs step 6b: carry lot lines or hydrants from sheet 6 (south side of Valley Avenue)).

sheet-11-2.description: An inset in the upper right of sheet 11, at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left, showing the blocks between North Third Street and North Second Street from Caldwell Avenue to Fairview Avenue on the north-western side of Hammonton. Blocks 106 to 109 and 42 hold frame dwellings, a few stores and sheds; land beyond is marked no exposure.
notes: Caldwell Avenue is modern Colwell Avenue.

100 ft. Three parts: part 1 Bellevue to Grape, 5th St/Liberty to Valley Av (Liberty junctions left out: drawn spacing disagrees with modern South Liberty Street by about 20 m; the sheet fits only at about 3.76 px/ft); part 2 inset: Caldwell (Colwell) and Fairview Avs between N 2nd and N 3rd; part 3 strip of lots on the north side of Valley Av east of Grape, drawn displaced below a heavy line, not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: strip of lots on the north side of Valley Avenue east of Grape Street (block 48, house numbers 231-383), drawn displaced below a heavy line (no street junction; Valley Avenue frontage only; needs step 6b: carry lot lines or hydrants from sheet 6 (south side of Valley Avenue)).

sheet-12-1.description: Main Road or White Horse Pike at the north-western edge of Hammonton, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left; the part covers the sheet above a heavy dividing line. The pike runs across the sheet; Fairview Avenue runs south from it and Basin Road north. Along the pike stand frame dwellings, the Fairview Hotel, a garage, a stone and cinder block building and an Italian hall; long narrow lots in blocks 45, 49, 52 and 53 extend back from the road.
notes: The pike is lettered Main Rd. or White Horse Pike.
Placed by a helmert transformation from the two junctions with the pike; low confidence.

100 ft. Two parts along Main Rd or White Horse Pike divided by a heavy line: part 1 at Fairview Av and Basin Rd (helmert on two junctions); part 2 at Bellevue Av (anchored on one junction, atlas scale, rotation -42).

sheet-12-2.description: Main Road or White Horse Pike at Bellevue Avenue, on the northern edge of Hammonton, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left below a heavy dividing line on sheet 12. Bellevue Avenue runs south from the pike down the sheet, Middle Road runs north at the right, and a private road leaves the pike and turns east to Bellevue Avenue. Along the pike are a fire department building, dwellings, a garage with gasoline tanks and a store; long lots in blocks 49 to 51 and 53 lie behind them.
notes: Anchored on the single junction of Bellevue Avenue with the pike, at the atlas scale and rotation; low confidence. Modern Bellevue Avenue meets the pike at two nodes about 65 m apart; the one on Bellevue's straight line was used.

100 ft. Two parts along Main Rd or White Horse Pike divided by a heavy line: part 1 at Fairview Av and Basin Rd (helmert on two junctions); part 2 at Bellevue Av (anchored on one junction, atlas scale, rotation -42).
